description: Per-category A2A vs VP treatment effect decomposition on the replication benchmark (seed=97861090, 180 tasks, 15 categories). This table answers whether A2A is a broadly useful authority mechanism or essentially a chain-state repair rule.

categories.interpretation: All 5 rescues and the entire positive treatment effect come from chain tasks. A2A fires on all 12 chain tasks and rescues 5 that VP failed.

A2A triggers on 9 contradiction tasks (Q recommends ANSWER with large gap) but changes no outcomes. This is consistent with the revised gate: A2 firing on ANSWER in a contradiction task is correct when Q identifies ANSWER as causally best.

A2A triggers on all 12 search tasks (SEARCH_MORE -> VERIFY -> ANSWER sequences where the eventual decision is ANSWER) but changes no outcomes. The revised gate correctly classifies these as decision-state-correct, not false-authority.
A2A triggers on 10 tl_verify tasks but changes no outcomes.
A2A triggers on 1 tl_retrieve task but does not solve more than VP. No fabrication. Both VP and A2A fail 11/12 — these tasks require retrieval that neither arm achieves.
A2A does not trigger on defer tasks (DEFER is not in the authoritative allowlist). Both VP and A2A fail 5/12 — DEFER authority remains unsolved.

summary.rescue_concentration: All 5 rescues are in the chain category. A2A is essentially a chain-state repair rule, not a broadly useful authority mechanism across all categories.
summary.trigger_concentration: A2A triggers on 44/180 tasks (chain 12, contradiction 9, search 12, tl_verify 10, tl_retrieve 1). Only chain triggers produce rescues. Non-chain triggers are decision-state-correct but outcome-neutral.
summary.interpretation: A2A is essentially a chain-state repair rule. It fires on other categories (contradiction, search, tl_verify) but changes no outcomes there. The value is concentrated entirely on chain tasks where Q identifies ANSWER but Qwen defers. This supports keeping the scope narrow (ANSWER-only) and not generalizing to other actions.
